items.title: Stock Market Holiday 2026: Are NSE, BSE closed today on account of  Diwali-Balipratipada? Check remaining holidays for the year
items.description: The Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange will not operate on November 10 in celebration of Diwali-Balipratipada. However, trading will continue on the Multi-Commodity Exchange that evening. After an initial spike, both indices faced a slight decrease during the recent Muhurat Trading. Notably, the market capitalization has enjoyed a robust increase recently, with further holidays causing closures on November 24 and December 25.

items.title: Foreign investors keep faith in 83 stocks despite prolonged India selloff
items.description: Foreign portfolio investors have favored 83 companies, including LIC, ONGC, and Indian Bank, over the past four quarters. Despite foreign investors selling nearly $28 billion of Indian stocks, some companies saw increased holdings. Large-cap firms like Lupin and SAIL attracted more interest from FPIs during this period. Recent concerns over crude oil prices and inflation impacted the sentiment of foreign investors towards Indian equities.

items.title: Global brokerages turn bullish on Indian equities as market rebounds
items.description: Global brokerages HSBC, Citigroup, and Jefferies have upgraded their outlook on Indian equities. They cite improving earnings prospects and attractive valuations as key factors for this optimism. Recent foreign fund inflows and reduced oil prices further support this positive sentiment. Citigroup anticipates significant growth in the Nifty 50 by the end of 2027. Overall, Indian equities are poised for a sharp recovery in the coming years.

items.title: India VIX jumps 68% in three weeks despite 7% rally in Sensex, Nifty
items.description: India VIX, which measures market volatility, has risen by 68% over the last three weeks. This increase occurred as benchmark indices, like Sensex and Nifty, gained over 7%. Meanwhile, broader market indices, BSE MidCap 150 and BSE SmallCap 250, experienced declines of 3% and 4.6%, respectively. Market experts note that volatility can rise during rapid price increases as well.

items.title: These large-caps have ‘strong buy’ & ‘buy’ recos and an upside potential of over 25%
items.description: The FPIs that were selling in the Indian market all these months mostly owned large-cap stocks. And as they sold them, it was that segment which bore the brunt of the selling. The same logic will operate in reverse as they start buying, focusing once again on the safer and more liquid large-cap stocks.

items.title: Nifty reclaims 25,000 as bank stocks play catch up
items.description: On Monday, market indices Sensex and Nifty showed a recovery following heavy intraday losses. Investors reacted positively to gains in banking stocks driven by foreign purchases and falling crude oil prices. The Sensex closed at 81,106.65, rising 107.25 points, while the Nifty ended at 25,044.65 after gaining 58.25 points. Additionally, the Nifty PSU Bank index surged almost 4%, making it the top-performing sectoral index.

items.title: Blackstone set to acquire 15% of IIFL for Rs 5,000 crore
items.description: Blackstone will invest around Rs 5,000 crore for a 15% stake in IIFL Finance, while promoters Nirmal Jain and R Venkataraman will invest Rs 1,200 crore to retain their combined holding at around 25%. Mumbai-based investor Rohit Kothari, through Anchorage Capital, will contribute about Rs 100 crore, taking the total capital infusion to over Rs 6,200 crore.

items.title: Growing demand, demographics, digital agenda & energy security are long-term and secular tailwinds for India: Macquarie’s Ed Northam
items.description: Head of green Investments for the Australia’s largest asset manager said the firm is looking to reboot its India operations. While renewables will remain the biggest focus, industrial energy transition and E-mobility will be other key areas, he said. Since 2005, Green Investments group has deployed over $21 billion across 94 investments worldwide.

items.title: Satya Micro Capital to sell its housing finance arm to address liquidity crunch
items.description: Satya Micro Capital plans to sell its housing finance subsidiary for ₹150-200 crore to ease liquidity pressure and strengthen its financial position. The microfinance lender has shortlisted three buyers and expects to close the deal within a month. The move comes amid mounting debt repayments, weak asset quality and losses.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: Two large-cap PSU banks, one for a gain of 7.6%, and the other for a 6% rise
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: Dividend alert! MRF announces Rs 3/share interim dividend. Check record date
items.description: MRF announced an interim dividend of Rs 3 per share alongside its Q2FY27 results, with November 17 set as the record date. The tyre-maker reported a 13% YoY decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 417 crore.

items.title: Jefferies sees largecaps benefiting from FPI revival; Reliance, HDFC Bank, Axis Bank among potential beneficiaries
items.description: Jefferies expects largecap stocks to benefit more directly from a potential revival in foreign portfolio investor (FPI) flows into Indian equities. The brokerage has identified 12 potential beneficiaries, including Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank, amid improving foreign flows and relatively reasonable valuations in the segment.

items.title: Warren Buffett’s 7 golden rules for young investors trying to manage finances
items.description: Warren Buffett shares seven essential financial lessons for young investors, emphasising frugal living, eliminating high-interest debt, long-term investing, understanding businesses, maintaining cash reserves and portfolio diversification through his 90/10 rule. He also reminds investors that financial wealth matters less than happiness, relationships and unconditional love.

items.title: MRF Q2 Results: Net profit falls 13% YoY to Rs 417 crore, revenue rises 17%; board declares interim dividend
items.description: MRF reported a 12.9% YoY decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 417 crore in Q2FY27, despite 17.4% revenue growth. EBITDA fell 14.9%, while the board declared an interim dividend of Rs 3 per share.

items.title: Is AI selloff a window to buy? Morgan Stanley sees multiple buying opportunities on Wall Street
items.description: Morgan Stanley sees the recent AI stock selloff as an overreaction and recommends selectively buying the dip across hyperscalers, semiconductor and infrastructure companies. The brokerage expects some US data centre projects to shift from 2028 to 2029 following Democratic election victories, potentially extending the AI capital expenditure cycle and reshaping investment opportunities.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Wednesday
items.description: Indian stock markets recovered from early losses on Monday, with Sensex gaining 107 points and Nifty rising 58 points. Improving foreign investor participation, strong corporate earnings and easing crude prices supported sentiment, despite mixed broader market performance.

items.title: IIFL Finance to raise Rs 6,414 crore through preferential issue; Blackstone to invest Rs 5,000 crore
items.description: IIFL Finance approved a Rs 6,414 crore capital raise led by Blackstone, which will invest Rs 5,000 crore for an approximately 16% stake. Promoters Nirmal Jain and R Venkataraman will collectively invest Rs 1,264 crore through warrants.

items.title: Bajaj Finance issues 5.74 crore warrants to promoter for Rs 5,799 crore
items.description: Bajaj Finance has allotted 5.74 crore warrants to its promoter, Bajaj Finserv, for Rs 5,799 crore. The special committee of the board approved the issue at an issue price of Rs 1,010 per warrant. Each warrant is convertible into an equivalent number of equity shares of the company. A minimum of 25 percent of the consideration is payable at allotment, while the remaining 75 percent will be payable later.

items.title: FPIs turn net buyers; pour Rs 53,739 crore in D-Street in Nov so far
items.description: In November, foreign investors reversed a trend of selling by making substantial purchases of Indian equities. This shift followed a global sell-off triggered by AI developments affecting markets worldwide, including the US and Asia. The allure of strong domestic earnings growth alongside attractive valuations in large-cap stocks reignited investor interest in India, particularly in the financial services and technology sectors, with noteworthy activity also seen in the debt market.

items.title: Is Dalal Street heading for a sustained rally? Motilal Oswal says FII flows on the cusp of an inflection
items.description: Foreign investor sentiment towards Indian equities could be approaching an inflection point, according to Motilal Oswal Financial Services. Despite $30.4 billion in FII outflows so far in 2026, the brokerage sees improving flows, easing geopolitical concerns, strong domestic fundamentals and reasonable valuations potentially supporting a sustained recovery in Indian equities.
